chunks: And there is no blame upon those who came to you to be carried, to whom you said, 'I cannot find anything with which to carry you,' so they turned away with their eyes overflowing with tears, grieving that they could not find what to spend.
ai.seo_question: Who are the people excused for not spending in the way of God due to lack of means?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the sincerity of the 'Mu'allafat Qulubuhim' or general companions who, despite their poverty, possessed genuine grief for not being able to contribute to the military expedition. It distinguishes their heartfelt remorse from the hypocrisy of those who withheld wealth out of stinginess, affirming that their emotional response served as proof of their faith. This context underscores the Islamic principle that intention and capacity are weighed together in divine judgment.
